name: Healthy Cities
line: The funded 2025–26 chapter of Bridge the Gap: twenty-six Delhi-NCR schools, and ten Green Fellows in eight states.
deck: One funded year of Bridge the Gap, taught as health rather than as ecology, plus a national fellowship that is the half of it happening outside Delhi.

figures.label: Students in the schools that ran it

how.p: The same subjects Bridge the Gap already teaches — air, water, waste, food, green cover — taught as what they do to the body of the person living with them. Five links, one argument, inside the school timetable rather than beside it.

A curriculum in Delhi-NCR schools, and the Green Fellowship: a national open call that funded ten people to pilot their own environment-health idea where they already live and work. The second strand is the only part of this that happens outside Delhi.

holes.what: The two modelled figures rest on two multipliers nothing we hold states as a fact: that a partner school has a roll of one to two thousand, and that the smallest of the ten fellows’ communities holds more than five thousand people. Both are the owner’s own reading of the schools and the ground, not a figure from a roll register or a census extract.
holes.unlocks: Roll numbers from the twenty-six schools, and a population for each of the ten communities. Either one turns a modelled span into something counted.

holes.what: It is one funded year, and nothing we hold says whether there is a second.
holes.unlocks: A renewal or an end date, which is the difference between a chapter that is running and one that has finished.
